articles.title: HAL to fully acquire Hatsoff Helicopter Training from CAE
articles.description: HAL Acquisition Hatsoff Helicopter Training: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) has announced the full acquisition of Hatsoff Helicopter Training from CAE, making it a 100%...
articles.articleText: Aviation 2 min read HAL to fully acquire Hatsoff Helicopter Training from CAE The acquisition will make Hatsoff a wholly owned subsidiary of HAL, giving the defence PSU full management control over its simulator-based military and civil helicopter pilot training business. ET Infra Desk ETInfra Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 10:51 AM IST The transaction is a related-party transaction under SEBI's listing regulations as HAL already holds a 50 per cent stake in Hatsoff. HAL said the transaction is not at arm's length.Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) has signed an agreement to acquire the remaining 50 per cent stake in Hatsoff Helicopter Training Pvt Ltd from Canada's CAE, the company said in a regulatory filing on Friday.HAL will acquire 3,84,04,205 equity shares, each with a face value of ₹10, from CAE. Following the transfer, Hatsoff will become a 100 per cent wholly owned subsidiary of HAL.Hatsoff currently operates as a 50:50 joint venture between HAL and CAE and provides military and civil helicopter pilot training through simulator-based facilities. Advt HAL stated that the acquisition will give it full management control over Hatsoff and streamline decision-making by converting the joint venture into a wholly owned subsidiary. The company's business is aligned with HAL's main line of operations, it said.The transaction is a related-party transaction under SEBI's listing regulations as HAL already holds a 50 per cent stake in Hatsoff. HAL said the transaction is not at arm's length.The defence public sector undertaking has received administrative approval from the Ministry of Defence's Department of Defence Production (MoD-DDP), with the concurrence of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), Ministry of Finance, for acquiring CAE's entire stake in the joint venture.The transaction is expected to be completed within 60 days from the signing of the share transfer agreement, HAL said.Hatsoff's businessHatsoff provides simulator-based helicopter pilot training to military and civil customers. Its customers include helicopter pilots from the Indian Air Force, Army, Navy, Coast Guard and Border Security Force, as well as civil helicopter operators such as Pawan Hans and Global Vectra.The company was incorporated on January 16, 2008. Its turnover rose to ₹80.95 crore in FY26 from ₹69.55 crore in FY25 and ₹66.49 crore in FY24.Hatsoff has an authorised capital of ₹76.84 crore and paid-up capital of ₹76.80 crore, according to HAL's filing. articles.title: Noel Tata seeks Tata Sons meeting video, minutes; questions legal opinions on Chandrasekaran reappointment
articles.description: Noel Tata requests video and minutes from Tata Sons meeting regarding N Chandrasekaran's reappointment amid controversy over legal opinions and governance issues.
articles.articleText: Corporate 3 min read Noel Tata seeks Tata Sons meeting video, minutes; questions legal opinions on Chandrasekaran reappointment Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has sought the video recording and minutes of the September 17 Tata Sons board meeting that reappointed N Chandrasekaran for another five years, executives said. He also questioned the process of obtaining legal opinions after the meeting and said he was not given adequate time to present his views. Kala Vijayraghavan & Maulik Vyas ET Bureau Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 08:00 AM IST From the Chandrachud report, the executives said, Noel Tata wanted to raise the points on casting vote and Tata Sons' articles of association (AOA) which, according to him, must be read in context of the original contents of the AOA and the changes made over a period of time.Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has written to the Tata Sons board, seeking details of the video recording and minutes of the September 17 meeting that decided to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as its chairman, executives familiar with the matter said.In the communication dated September 30, he also called out the manner in which the board submitted two legal opinions to validate Chandrasekaran's reappointment after the meeting in which the decision was taken. Noel Tata said he was not given an adequate opportunity at the meeting to detail specific points from the legal view he obtained from former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud, the executives said. According to them, Noel Tata claimed that the resolution was passed as a "debrief from the NRC (nomination and remuneration committee)." Advt From the Chandrachud report, the executives said, Noel Tata wanted to raise the points on casting vote and Tata Sons' articles of association (AOA) which, according to him, must be read in context of the original contents of the AOA and the changes made over a period of time.Noel Tata tabled the Chandrachud report before the Tata Sons board on September 17 and, citing that, argued that the casting vote of the Tata Sons chairman could not be used to override the specific affirmative voting rights provided to Tata Trusts' nominee directors.Listing matter A public battle broke out on September 17 after the board of Tata Sons reappointed executive chairman Chandrasekaran for five years by a majority 4-1 decision. Noel Tata, chairman of the Tata Trusts that own the majority of shares in Tata Group holding company, cast the sole vote against the resolution. Venu Srinivasan, the other trust nominee on the board, favoured the reappointment.The meeting took place in the backdrop of a decision by the Reserve Bank of India, which rejected Tata Sons' request to stay private and unlisted. The regulator clarified that its rules for shadow banks of a certain size, which are required to be publicly held, would be applicable to the company.Tata Sons said its board resolved by a majority decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran as executive chairman and also resolved to "initiate steps to comply with the applicable RBI guidelines." Tata Trusts publicly said it considered the board decision on Chandrasekaran's appointment as illegal.Independent counsel Vyapak Desai said there was no legal requirement to provide the video recording of a board meeting to a director. Advt "A director does not have an unfettered right to obtain the full copy of the video recording of the board meeting. But secretarial guidance and corporate governance measures indicate that the director may be allowed to view specific recordings to verify the discussion and give comments, if any, to draft minutes before finalisation," Desai said. "The recording, however, should be preserved till completion of the audit to ensure sanctity."Tata Trusts and Tata Sons did not comment.Conflicting legal opinionsThe Chandrachud report that Noel Tata tabled at the board meeting said a casting vote could not create a majority where the articles of association required a separate majority from a particular group of directors. In that reading, a deadlock between the two trust nominees cannot be overcome simply by invoking the chairman's casting vote, he opined.Tata Sons' board also obtained legal opinion before the board meeting from senior counsel Sudipto Sarkar, who said, on a plain reading of Article 121 of the AOA on voting rules, the chairman's casting vote could be invoked in two situations: where there is an equality of votes by the trust nominees or where there is an equality of votes after considering the votes cast by all directors. Accordingly, the expression "in the case of an equality of votes" may reasonably be construed as applying to either situation.Soon after the board meeting, Tata Sons obtained legal opinions from former Chief Justice of India UU Lalit and retired Supreme Court Justice BN Srikrishna. Their reports upheld the validity of the September 17 board resolution, finding that the chairman's casting vote under Article 121 was properly used to break the deadloc

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh announces ₹11,085 crore rural infrastructure push under Palle Panduga-3.0
articles.description: Discover Andhra Pradesh's ambitious ₹11,085 crore initiative for rural infrastructure at the Palle Panduga-3.0 event, aiming for extensive road construction and housing...
articles.articleText: Rural Infrastructure 1 min read Andhra Pradesh announces ₹11,085 crore rural infrastructure push under Palle Panduga-3.0 The third phase will cover 9,500 km of BT roads, 22,000 mini Gokulams, 50,000 acres of horticulture expansion and 1,000 km of magic drains, alongside housing and welfare initiatives. Sandeep Raghavan TNN Updated On Sep 30, 2026 at 03:11 PM IST Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy CM K Pawan Kalyan announce rural infrastructure and development initiatives.Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu and his deputy K Pawan Kalyan announced a slew of infrastructure, housing, agriculture and welfare initiatives at the Palle Panduga-3.0 event in Ramapuram village, Nellore district’s Varikuntapadu mandal.Naidu said 28,000 house-site pattas had recently been distributed in Visakhapatnam, with another 24,000 beneficiaries set to receive titles in Vijayawada under the ‘Mee Illu–Mee Hakku’ programme.He announced the launch of a Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub on October 2 with Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and the groundbreaking for three lakh houses on October 4 with Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Advt Naidu said the state was courting investments in space, aerospace, semiconductors, green energy, quantum computing and data centres to create long-term opportunities for youth.Under Palle Panduga-3.0, the state is taking up 15,500 km of BT and CC roads, including 6,000 km of concrete roads, at a cost of ₹2,700 crore. Naidu said 6,500km of rural roads had already been completed in two years.Pawan Kalyan said the ₹11,085-crore third phase would cover 9,500 km of BT roads, 22,000 mini Gokulams, 50,000 acres of horticulture expansion and 1,000 km of magic drains. The Adavi Tallibata programme has added over 1,500 km of roads to tribal settlements.SPS Nellore district will receive nearly ₹520 crore. Udayagiri constituency has already received ₹121 crore for 115 km of roads, 1,200 water ponds and 348 mini Gokulams.The state has also sanctioned ₹52 crore for 381 Sujala Sravanthi works to tackle fluoride contamination, ₹2.5 crore for an Udayagiri Fort access road, and ₹3.5 crore for a road serving salt producers in Gokulapalli. articles.description: Birla Evara: New 25-acre residential township by Birla Estates in Kodathi, Bangalore. 1,594 units from Rs 77 Lakh. 13 towers, 80% open space.
articles.articleText: UpcomingBIRLA SARJAPUR ROAD — New Project Coming Up in Kodathi, BangaloreBirla Evara Coming to Kodathi: 1,600-Unit Township on Sarjapur RoadBirla Evara is a new launch project by Birla Estates at Kodathi, off Sarjapur Road, East Bangalore. The project spans 25 acres and comprises 13 towers with 1,594 ultra-luxury apartments in 1, 2, 3, 3.5, and 4 BHK configurations. Prices start at Rs 77 Lakhs.Scale and DesignThe project offers 80% open spaces with 20% of land used for construction. Apartment sizes range from 449 sq ft to 1,630 sq ft. The project features Vaastu-compliant towers and amenities including a clubhouse and an in-house temple.Location and ConnectivityThe project is located at Kodathi village, Varthur Hobli, Bangalore East Taluk, Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka - 560035. Kodathi is about 20 kilometers from Bangalore city center. The location is well connected with Electronic City (6 km), Outer Ring Road (8 km), and RGA Tech Park (5 km).Kodathi Gate is located near Wipro SEZ, RGA Tech Park, and the Outer Ring Road. Frequent BMTC buses serve the area, making daily commutes easy. The closest train station is Karmelaram Railway Station, 3.5 km away on Sarjapur Main Road.The project is in proximity to the Ibbaluru metro station, with the Red Line (Hebbal-Sarjapura Line) proposed to increase local connectivity. Ibbaluru is an interchange point for Namma Metro's Phase 3A, which will connect the Outer Ring Road (ORR) to the Blue Line.About Birla EstatesBirla Estates was established in 2016 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Century Textiles and Industries Limited. The developer is crafting 1–4 BHK homes and mixed-use townships in Mumbai, Bengaluru, NCR, Pune, and more. The company majorly operates in Bangalore, Mumbai and Gurugram NCR.Birla Estates develops premium and higher mid-income residential housing through both owned land parcels and joint ventures with landowners. With a legacy spanning over 125 years through its parent entities, Birla is known for its commitment to innovation, transparency, and timely delivery.TimelineThe project is RERA-approved and set to launch in March 2025, with construction starting in May 2025 and completion expected by December 2031.Regulatory DetailsThe starting price for 1 BHK is Rs 77 Lakhs, with options up to Rs 2.95 Cr for larger configurations. The project address is Kodathi village, Varthur Hobli, Off Sarjapur Road, Bangalore East Taluk, Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka - 560035. articles.title: SPVs set up under smart cities mission in Tamil Nadu reduced to funding conduits: CAG report
articles.description: Smart Cities Mission Tamil Nadu: A recent CAG report reveals that Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) set up under Tamil Nadu's Smart Cities Mission have devolved into mere funding...
articles.articleText: Smart City 2 min read SPVs set up under smart cities mission in Tamil Nadu reduced to funding conduits: CAG report Critics have raised concerns about Tamil Nadu's Smart Cities Mission, highlighting that special purpose vehicles (SPVs) have become mere financial channels rather than independent entities. Public funding was misallocated to regular municipal projects outside of the planned development areas. Additionally, many expensive commercial projects sit unused, not bringing in the profits they promised. PTI Published On Sep 9, 2026 at 09:16 AM IST Representative AI imageCHENNAI: The SPVs set up under the SCM in Tamil Nadu have been reduced to mere funding conduits, with public funds routinely diverted to routine municipal works outside designated development zones, according to a CAG report tabled in the Assembly on Tuesday.The performance audit on the implementation of the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) in Tamil Nadu revealed that several multi-crore commercial ventures, including multi-level car parking facilities and modernised markets, are lying idle or abandoned, failing to generate projected revenues.The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) report noted that Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in the state lacked the operational independence mandated by mission guidelines. The paid-up capital of the SPVs was restricted to just Rs 10 lakh instead of the mandatory Rs 200 crore, and full-time chief executive officers were not appointed in six of the seven sampled cities, leaving municipal commissioners with conflicting roles. Consequently, the SPVs functioned without operational autonomy, merely financing projects pushed by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). Advt Across the sampled cities, 70 projects involving an expenditure of Rs 655.43 crore were executed outside approved Area-Based Development (ABD) zones. Furthermore, 44 unplanned projects worth Rs 623.86 crore were taken up, with 21 of them executed entirely outside ABD limits.In Tirunelveli, the SPV dropped a planned Rs 8.25-crore electric vehicle project and instead diverted Rs 16.50 crore to procure street sweepers and jet-rodding machines for the city corporation. Administrative and office expense funds were also diverted across cities to clear corporation power dues, settle staff salaries, and purchase vehicles.The audit highlighted that major commercial assets built to ensure the financial sustainability of the SPVs have failed to take off. Multi-Level Car Parking (MLCP) facilities and commercial complexes constructed across four cities at a cost of Rs 115.92 crore could not be put to full use due to incomplete installations of lifts, automation systems, and access ramps.In Madurai, a tourism plaza built at a cost of Rs 2.62 crore has remained idle and unmaintained for more than three years. In Salem, only 39 of the 202 shops in the redeveloped Old Bus Stand, constructed at an outlay of Rs 104.53 crore, were leased out. Advt The CAG also red-flagged that Rs 57.72 crore in revenue generated from completed smart city assets was retained entirely by the municipal corporations rather than credited to the SPVs, eroding their long-term financial viability. articles.title: Railways prioritises ₹9,000 crore Rangpo-Gangtok rail link to connect Sikkim capital
articles.description: Gangtok Railway Link: The Indian Railway Ministry has prioritized a massive ₹9,000 crore project to establish a 34-km rail link between Rangpo and Gangtok, aiming to enhance...
articles.articleText: Railways 1 min read Railways prioritises ₹9,000 crore Rangpo-Gangtok rail link to connect Sikkim capital The 34-km line has been taken up by the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan’s Network Planning Group, with the Railways planning it as an extension of the Sivok-Rangpo project targeted for completion by December 2027. Dipak K Dash TNN Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 02:00 PM IST The proposed Rangpo-Gangtok railway link will extend rail connectivity to Sikkim’s capital through the Himalayan terrain.In a push to bring Sikkim’s capital, Gangtok, on the railway map, the Railway Ministry has prioritised the plan for a 34-km rail link between Rangpo and Gangtok, estimated to cost around ₹9,000 crore.TOI has learnt that the proposed link was taken up by the Integrated Multimodal Network Planning Group (NPG), the multi-modal evaluation body under the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, last week.The proposed line will extend the railway network from Rangpo to Gangtok once the ongoing Sivok-Rangpo link project is completed. The move comes as the railways targets completion of the long-delayed Sivok-Rangpo railway line by Dec 2027. Advt The 44.5-km Sivok-Rangpo line, being built at an estimated cost of ₹17,124 crore, will provide the first direct rail connectivity to Sikkim. The project has faced delays because of the challenging Himalayan terrain, which requires the construction of several tunnels and major bridges.The railways have been working to extend rail connectivity to the capitals of the north-eastern states. At present, four state capitals in the region have rail connectivity. With Sivok-Rangpo and the proposed Rangpo-Gangtok link, Sikkim would become the next state in the region to get a railway connection to its capital.Officials said the Rangpo-Gangtok extension is being examined now so that work on the next leg can be taken forward without a significant gap after the Sivok-Rangpo section becomes operational. articles.title: Concrete foundations for stronger economy: Infrastructure and cement leading India’s transformation
articles.description: India's infrastructure push is expected to drive cement demand and capacity expansion over the coming years, with sustainability, green technologies and decarbonisation...
articles.articleText: Economy 5 min read Concrete foundations for stronger economy: Infrastructure and cement leading India’s transformation India's infrastructure push is expected to drive cement demand and capacity expansion over the coming years, with sustainability, green technologies and decarbonisation emerging as key priorities for the industry's long-term growth. Shrivats Singhania ETManufacturing Published On Aug 1, 2026 at 10:30 AM IST Indias infrastructure and cement sectors are set to play a critical role in supporting economic growth and sustainable development.With its nominal GDP at around $4.15 trillion at present, India is aiming to become a $10 trillion economy in less than 10 years. This giant leap will be fuelled by an equally noticeable quantum jump by the infrastructure sector.Within that larger picture, India’s cement industry is expected to play a leading role, because, the government has aimed its guns to boost investments in roads, railways, urban development, housing and industrial projects, all of which will spur demand for construction materials; cement in particular. Advt Together, infrastructure and cement form the physical foundation of India's economic transformation, driving investment, employment and productivity while enabling sustainable long-term growth; as these two sectors are deeply interconnected.Morgan Stanley projects India’s infrastructure investment to rise from 5.3 per cent of GDP in FY24 to 6.5 per cent by FY29. Although the cement industry’s contribution to India’s GDP is less than two per cent, being a foundational sector, it has a huge GDP multiplier effect which ultimately increases its contribution to it.This makes the cement a crucial driver and a foundation of India’s growth, just the way it is in a building. In 2026, the country became the world’s second-largest cement producer, producing 490 million tonnes, growing by nine per cent over the previous year. This was roughly eight per cent of the world's total cement-making capacity.The domestic cement industry’s growth is being pushed by the government’s infrastructure push which is creating demand. In the last few years, the government has allocated record budgets for roads, railways, logistics, and industrial corridors, and pushed for increased housing, especially in Tier II and III towns. In the recent Union Budget, the government allocated ₹3.09 lakh crore for the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to build more expressways.Housing and construction accounts for 60 per cent of all cement demand. This is also being fuelled by government housing schemes in rural and urban areas, both in commercial and residential real estate. Advt Obviously, this augurs well for the cement industry. To match this spurt in demand, the cement industry is responding proactively by setting up new capacity. Looking at the growth trends and increasing demand, the industry, with a current installed capacity of about 700 MTPA, is planning to add about 170 million tonnes of new production capacity between 2026 and 2028.According to CRISIL Ratings, Indian cement companies are planning to spend ₹1.2 lakh crore between FY26 and FY28, which means a 75 per cent jump in capacity addition compared to the previous three fiscal years.This makes the next phase of growth for Indian cement very critical because going forward, the growth has to be responsible and sustainable. Three forces will determine the shape of the cement industry in our march to 2030 when the cement industry has a target to scale its production capacity to over 850 MTPA to meet surging infrastructure demand as well as a targeted reduction in carbon emissions.These include consolidation, Green Transition with new concepts like Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), blended fuels, Carbon Credits and alternative fuels, and these will be the new code of conduct for the industry.The industry also has to draw a growth strategy that is dotted with shields for geopolitical risks like the current wars, fuel shocks and import dependence on coal and petcoke. It will also have to look at efficient cost structures, renewable energy integration, AI adoption and regional presence. So, while numbers and volumes are important, future growth will be determined by quality and efficiency.An important dialogue that has emerged and will be a driving force for our future growth is sustainability. Going forward, everything will be seen through green eyes and how companies and being responsible to the environment.With the industry moving towards green cement, using green inputs and recycling industrial waste like ash from power plants, instead of raw limestone is fast becoming the norm. This has a significant impact in reducing carbon emissions and protecting the environment. To reduce energy costs and greenhouse gases, companies are exploring captive wind and solar power plants.One thing is clear. To remain an active player in the future, the industry has to build cleaner, efficient, and long term.A

articles.articleText: Ports and Shipping 5 min read Priya Blue, India’s biggest ship recycler, becomes target of online fake news The company says reports alleging sanctions breaches and money laundering were published across multiple websites, while reviews by legal firms found no evidence backing the allegations. ET Infra Desk ETInfra Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 05:54 PM IST Read by 100 Professionals The case of Priya Blue Industries and Best Oasis, family-owned businesses led by Sanjay Mehta and his son Gaurav Mehta, shows how this pattern unfolds in practice.Gujarat-based Priya Blue Group, India’s biggest ship recycler by number of ships and tonnage, and its Dubai-based unit Best Oasis Ltd, which buys ships for recycling, have become the target of reports published online by rogue websites seeking to tarnish their reputation by alleging money laundering, sanctions breaches, and dealings involving sanctioned vessels.Fake stories, allegations and reputation attacks are not new. For years, politicians and celebrities have been among the most visible targets. Advt What is changing is the target's profile. The same tactics are increasingly reaching businesses and family-owned corporate groups that may not be widely known to the public but whose reputations are central to their ability to operate.These attacks often follow a pattern. A story carrying serious allegations against a company appears online. It uses genuine details about a company, its owners, locations, transactions or business history, and then builds an unverified or misleading allegation around those facts.Because the background information is accurate, the accusation can appear credible as well. The reader recognises the names and facts as genuine and may therefore assume that the accusation based on them has also been validated.The pattern becomes more concerning when the same story is published by the same source across several unrelated websites in different countries, often under slightly altered headlines or bylines.To an outside reader, this can create the impression of multiple independent reports, even though the articles may trace back to one person or content supplier. Many of these platforms have limited readership, little visible editorial structure and no easily identifiable newsroom or responsible editor, making it difficult to establish who verified the allegations or to obtain a meaningful response once the story is challenged. Advt The purpose of such an attack is to tarnish a company’s reputation, weaken trust in its name and disrupt or damage its business relationships and commercial standing. In today’s digital footprint, anything published online can become part of what customers, banks, investors and business partners find about a company, whether the information is true, false or never independently verified.The case of Priya Blue Industries and Best Oasis, family-owned businesses led by Sanjay Mehta and his son Gaurav Mehta, shows how this pattern unfolds in practice.Questions over credibilityArticles alleging money laundering, sanctions breaches, and dealings involving sanctioned vessels appeared on websites in several countries, including the US, the UK, and India.Despite appearing under different publication names and in different parts of the world, the reports were strikingly similar. The allegations followed the same sequence, with identical text and photographs, and only the headlines changed.There was no clearly identifiable journalist taking responsibility for the reporting. Some articles were attributed simply to a “Web Desk” or “Monitoring Desk”.Official records and documents reviewed by ET Infra relating to the allegations did not show any criminal or money-laundering investigations against the group or its principals of the kind mentioned in the articles.The material reviewed also did not establish that Priya Blue, Best Oasis, its promoter Sanjay Mehta and his son Gaurav Mehta were involved in the sanctions-related conduct alleged in the reports.No evidence backing allegationsHolman Fenwick Willan LLP (HFW), an international law firm, has certified that there is no criminal record or ongoing criminal investigation against the Mehta family in Dubai.Crawford Bayley & Co., a reputable Indian law firm, has certified that the Mehta family are not shareholders or directors of the recycling companies named in the articles alleging that they have recycled sanctioned ships.Besides, the vessels named ‘Blue Lady’ and ‘Oriental Nicety’ were recycled by Priya Blue Industries strictly in accordance with permissions granted by the Supreme Court of India and relevant Indian authorities, including the Gujarat Maritime Board, Gujarat Pollution Control Board, and Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, according to Crawford Bayley & Co.Business transactions involving the company are being carried out through the required commercial and regulatory process and executed through banking channels and in USD, reflecting full compliance, sources said.A Police r

articles.title: Chandigarh civic body turns C&D waste into over ₹50 lakh revenue in six months
articles.description: Chandigarh MC processed 1,500–2,700 MT of C&D waste from April–September, earning Rs 50.5 lakh by selling recycled sand, bricks and aggregate.
articles.articleText: infrastructure 1 min read Chandigarh civic body turns C&D waste into over ₹50 lakh revenue in six months The Municipal Corporation in Chandigarh has turned construction and demolition waste into sand, bricks, and aggregate. From April to September, the civic body received over 2,700 metric tonnes of waste, which is processed for reuse. The authority earned between Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh monthly by selling these materials to government agencies. Despite multiple attempts to find a private bidder, the facility operates on a no-profit, no-loss basis. Deepak Yadav TNN Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 01:00 PM IST Representative AI imageCHANDIGARH: The MC has processed and dispatched much of the construction and demolition (C&D) waste it received, converting it into sand, bricks and aggregate (granular material made from crushed or processed construction debris). The civic body received between 1,500 metric tonnes (MT) and over 2,700 MT of C&D waste from across the city from April to September.Also, since the MC could not find a bidder to run the C&D waste plant, it is operating the facility on its own. The authority is collecting the waste through multiple designated C&D waste collection centres. Advt As per the MC, the authority earned around Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh each month from April to September. In total, the MC collected around Rs 50.5 lakh in the first six months of the current financial year by selling products made from C&D waste.“Around 23 employees have been hired to run the C&D waste plant in the absence of a private bidder. The MC engineering department is running the C&D waste plant on a no-profit, no-loss basis. Engineering officers are monitoring the work daily and submitting daily collection, processing and dispatch reports to their seniors,” sources told TOI.Sources also said that the articles made from C&D waste are sold to government agencies, which are using the material in ongoing construction works. “As construction material is quite expensive these days, the MC is getting many orders for these items from government agencies,” sources said.The civic body has turned down a proposal to consider or accept a single tender to run the C&D waste plant. It will prepare a new RFP. The tender to run the C&D plant has been floated four times, but no bidder responded. articles.title: ED arrests Ozone Urbana Infra Developer's CMD in ₹927.22 crore homebuyer alleged fraud case
articles.description: The Enforcement Directorate has arrested S Vasudevan, CMD of Ozone Urbana Infra Developers, for allegedly defrauding homebuyers of ₹927.22 crore. Ongoing investigations reveal...
articles.articleText: Regulatory 3 min read ED arrests Ozone Urbana Infra Developer's CMD in ₹927.22 crore homebuyer alleged fraud case Vasudevan was arrested on September 30 under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with the money laundering investigation being conducted against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and Others. ANI Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 08:12 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday said it had arrested S Vasudevan, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) and promoter of Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, in connection with an alleged homebuyer fraud case worth Rs 927.22 crore.Vasudevan was arrested on September 30 under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with the money laundering investigation being conducted against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and Others.The Enforcement Directorate said the arrest followed an ongoing investigation which revealed that Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, along with Vasudevan (main promoter), has defrauded the home buyers to the tune of Rs 927.22 crores and did not deliver possession of apartments and units against the money, thereby dishonestly retaining and diverting the funds. Advt ED's Bengaluru Zonal Office arrested Vasudevan and subsequently produced him before a special court in Bengaluru on October 1, which granted 14 days' ED custody for further investigation.ED investigation was initiated based on multiple First Information Reports (FIRs) under sections 419, 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at various police stations of Bengaluru City against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and its promoters. Further, an FIR was also registered against the company and its promoter by the Central Bureau of Investigation on the direction of the Supreme Court.ED said the main allegation against the company Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd is that it has defaulted in completion of construction of the project in time and failed to hand over the possession to the customers."It is alleged that the company induced the gullible customer by offering to pay pre-construction EMIs till handing over the possession of the flat to homebuyers. However, it has failed to honour its commitments and did not complete the project and flats. The builder neither delivered possession of the residential units to homebuyers nor refunded their deposited amount and misappropriated the entire upfront booking amount/loan amount," said the ED in a statement. Advt Earlier, ED's Bangalore zonal office had conducted search operations under section 17 of PMLA, 2002 on August 1 last year in this case and seized various incriminating documents from various premises."Further investigation has revealed that Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd along with Vasudevan (main promoter) have defrauded the home buyers to the tune of Rs 927.22 Crores and did not deliver possession of apartments and units against the said money, thereby dishonestly retaining and diverting the funds."Based on the investigation conducted and the material gathered, ED said it had earlier issued a Provisional Attachment Order on October 4 last year, provisionally attaching immovable properties having a total value of Rs 423.378 crores under the provisions of the PMLA.A parallel investigation has been initiated under the provisions of the PMLA, 2002 on the basis of three different FIRs registered by the CBI, New Delhi, against Ozone Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, Ozone Realtors Pvt Ltd and Ozone Projects Pvt Ltd for defrauding the homebuyers.ED said Vasudevan is the common director in all three companies under investigation.As per the ED, the arrest of Vasudevan has been effected pursuant to the material gathered during the investigation and is aimed at further investigating the generation, diversion, layering and utilisation of the Proceeds of Crime, including the role of the promoter and the various group entities and persons through whom the funds were routed. articles.title: Ranchi civic body to install 5,300 LED street lights across city
articles.description: Ranchi Municipal Corporation to install 5,300 LED street lights before festivals, adding to 60,000 existing lights, with 3-year maintenance and rapid repairs citywide.
articles.articleText: Outdoor Lighting 2 min read Ranchi civic body to install 5,300 LED street lights across city The civic body has floated a tender inviting eligible companies to supply, install, test and commission LED street lights of 75 W, 90 W and 120 W capacities. The contract also includes related services and three years of comprehensive maintenance. Kelly Kislaya TNN Published On Sep 19, 2026 at 07:06 PM IST RANCHI: With the festive season approaching, the Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) has initiated steps to illuminate dark spots and narrow lanes across the city by installing 5,300 new LED street lights.The civic body has floated a tender inviting eligible companies to supply, install, test and commission LED street lights of 75 W, 90 W and 120 W capacities. The contract also includes related services and three years of comprehensive maintenance.The new lights will supplement the existing network of around 60,000 street lights across Ranchi. Sourabh Keshri, assistant engineer in RMC’s lights section, said the energy department had already installed poles in previously unlit lanes to ensure that no dark spots remained within the civic body’s jurisdiction before the festivities.Officials said regular surveys and maintenance work were also being carried out to keep existing street lights functional. As many as 28 dedicated teams have been deployed across all 53 wards to patrol neighbourhoods, identify faulty fixtures, address public complaints and install replacement lights wherever necessary.The move follows an internal review meeting held at the RMC headquarters earlier this month. During the meeting, officials noted that the municipal helpline receives more than 1,000 complaints related to faulty street lights every month. Most complaints, they said, are resolved within 48 hours.Additional municipal commissioner Sanjay Kumar said, “Footfall increases significantly during the upcoming festivals, making effective street lighting essential for public convenience, safety and smooth traffic movement.”Kumar has directed the electrical branch teams to work with promptness and coordination to prevent prolonged outages on major roads, at intersections, in market areas, public spaces and residential zones.He also stressed the need for proactive patrolling to identify structural faults at an early stage. Officials have been instructed to treat every complaint seriously, ensure quality repairs and implement permanent solutions in areas reporting recurring technical problems. articles.articleText: Construction of houses for Wayanad rehabilitation to be completed by Oct-end: Minister The construction of homes in the Wayanad rehabilitation township is on track, with a completion date set for the end of October. articles.title: Chandigarh civic body turns C&D waste into over ₹50 lakh revenue in six months
articles.description: Chandigarh MC processed 1,500–2,700 MT of C&D waste from April–September, earning Rs 50.5 lakh by selling recycled sand, bricks and aggregate.
articles.articleText: infrastructure 1 min read Chandigarh civic body turns C&D waste into over ₹50 lakh revenue in six months The Municipal Corporation in Chandigarh has turned construction and demolition waste into sand, bricks, and aggregate. From April to September, the civic body received over 2,700 metric tonnes of waste, which is processed for reuse. The authority earned between Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh monthly by selling these materials to government agencies. Despite multiple attempts to find a private bidder, the facility operates on a no-profit, no-loss basis. Deepak Yadav TNN Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 01:00 PM IST Representative AI imageCHANDIGARH: The MC has processed and dispatched much of the construction and demolition (C&D) waste it received, converting it into sand, bricks and aggregate (granular material made from crushed or processed construction debris). The civic body received between 1,500 metric tonnes (MT) and over 2,700 MT of C&D waste from across the city from April to September.Also, since the MC could not find a bidder to run the C&D waste plant, it is operating the facility on its own. The authority is collecting the waste through multiple designated C&D waste collection centres. Advt As per the MC, the authority earned around Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh each month from April to September. In total, the MC collected around Rs 50.5 lakh in the first six months of the current financial year by selling products made from C&D waste.“Around 23 employees have been hired to run the C&D waste plant in the absence of a private bidder. The MC engineering department is running the C&D waste plant on a no-profit, no-loss basis. Engineering officers are monitoring the work daily and submitting daily collection, processing and dispatch reports to their seniors,” sources told TOI.Sources also said that the articles made from C&D waste are sold to government agencies, which are using the material in ongoing construction works. “As construction material is quite expensive these days, the MC is getting many orders for these items from government agencies,” sources said.The civic body has turned down a proposal to consider or accept a single tender to run the C&D waste plant. It will prepare a new RFP. The tender to run the C&D plant has been floated four times, but no bidder responded. articles.title: Allcargo Logistics names Vijay Nehra as MD designate; Ketan Kulkarni gets Group growth role
articles.description: Allcargo Logistics has appointed Vijay Nehra as Chief Transformation Officer and Managing Director Designate, effective October 1. Ketan Kulkarni transitions to Chief Growth...
articles.articleText: Logistics 1 min read Allcargo Logistics names Vijay Nehra as MD designate; Ketan Kulkarni gets Group growth role Nehra will take over as MD & Chief Transformation Officer from January 1, 2027, while Kulkarni will become Chief Growth Officer of Allcargo Group. ET Infra Desk ETInfra Published On Sep 29, 2026 at 11:19 PM IST Vijay Nehra, Chief Transformation Officer & MD Designate, Allcargo LogisticsAllcargo Logistics on Tuesday appointed Vijay Nehra as Chief Transformation Officer and Managing Director Designate, effective October 1, as part of a leadership transition following the restructuring of the Allcargo Group.Nehra will work with the existing leadership during the transition and is set to assume the role of Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer from January 1, 2027, subject to shareholder approvals.Ketan Kulkarni, currently MD & CEO of Allcargo Logistics, will move to the group-level role of Chief Growth Officer from January 1. He will oversee sales and marketing initiatives across the group, with a focus on emerging industries and new growth opportunities. Advt Both Nehra and Kulkarni will report to Punit Misra, Chief Business Officer, Allcargo Group.Nehra has held leadership roles across supply chain, sales, finance and general management, including stints at Hindustan Unilever, Indiabulls and Ozone Pharma. He holds a postgraduate programme in management from ISB Hyderabad and a Bachelor of Nautical Sciences from T.S. Chanakya, University of Mumbai.The transition follows the group’s restructuring after the demerger, with Allcargo Logistics continuing to focus on its domestic supply chain business, including express distribution, air freight, e-commerce logistics and first- and last-mile delivery. articles.title: Uttarakhand GST department recovers ₹2.25 crore as tax evasion from Eden Senior Living & Wellness
articles.description: Uttarakhand GST SIB recovered Rs 2.25 crore from Eden Senior Living after inspection found alleged GST irregularities on flat sales; total liability Rs 12.5 crore.
articles.articleText: Regulatory 1 min read Uttarakhand GST department recovers ₹2.25 crore as tax evasion from Eden Senior Living & Wellness Following a thorough inspection of Eden Senior Living & Wellness by the Uttarakhand tax department, it became evident that discrepancies in GST payments had occurred. The company responded by depositing Rs 2.25 crore towards its identified tax liability of Rs 12.50 crore, mainly stemming from improper input tax credit usage. Pankul Sharma TNN Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 10:47 AM IST DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand tax department has recovered Rs 2.25 crore from Eden Senior Living & Wellness, a private real estate and wellness company operating an assisted-living facility for senior citizens, after alleged irregularities were detected in the payment of GST on flat sales, officials said.Special Investigation Branch (SIB) of the department inspected the company’s premises on Thursday, with the survey continuing on Friday. Officials said the company had discharged its GST liability on the sale of flats by using input tax credit (ITC) claimed on construction-related purchases, instead of paying the liability in cash. Advt The department assessed the company’s total tax liability at Rs 12.50 crore, following which the company deposited Rs 2.25 crore in the state exchequer and its directors sought time to pay the remaining amount.Deputy commissioner Suresh Kumar told TOI that the company was not legally permitted to use ITC for the liability in question. “To substantiate the irregularities, the investigating team collected documents, forms and information from Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA), Mussoorie Dehradun Development Authority (MDDA), district magistrate’s office, mining section and other departments,” Kumar said, adding that the team also seized records relating to the company’s business activities.Based on an analysis of data available on the GST portal and the documents collected during the inspection, the company’s directors, legal advisers and other representatives present during the investigation admitted to the tax-payment error, Kumar said.The investigation team included deputy commissioner Suresh Kumar, assistant commissioner Krishna Kumar and officials TR Chinyal, Alisha Bisht, Kanchan Thapa and Asad Ahmed.Eden Senior Living and Wellness, located in Purkul, offers studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom apartments for senior citizens. articles.title: Hindustan Zinc's refined metal production rises 7% to record 264 kt in Q2 FY27
articles.description: Refined zinc output rose 5% to 212 kt, lead 14% to 51 kt and silver production increased 20% to 173 metric tonnes.
articles.articleText: Construction 1 min read Hindustan Zinc's refined metal production rises 7% to record 264 kt in Q2 FY27 Refined zinc output rose 5% to 212 kt, lead 14% to 51 kt and silver production increased 20% to 173 metric tonnes. ETManufacturing Desk ETManufacturing Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 05:25 PM IST The company said refined metal production was supported by additional capacity unlocked through debottlenecking projects at Chanderiya and Dariba, along with the 160 ktpa roaster at Debari and plant availability.Hindustan Zinc Ltd on Saturday announced record refined metal production for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27).The company said mined metal production stood at 271 kt in Q2 FY27, up 5 per cent YoY, driven by higher ore production. Saleable metal production increased 7 per cent YoY to 264 kt during the quarter.Refined zinc production rose 5 per cent YoY to 212 kt, while refined lead production increased 14 per cent to 51 kt. Silver production stood at 173 metric tonnes, up 20 per cent YoY, in line with the company's production plan. Advt The company said refined metal production was supported by additional capacity unlocked through debottlenecking projects at Chanderiya and Dariba, along with the 160 ktpa roaster at Debari and plant availability.First-half production hits recordsFor the first half of FY27, Hindustan Zinc's mined metal production rose 3 per cent YoY to 539 kt, marking the sixth consecutive year of record first-half mined metal production.Refined metal production reached its highest-ever first-half level at 524 kt, up 6 per cent YoY. Silver production increased 10 per cent YoY to 321 metric tonnes, while wind power generation rose 8 per cent to 288 million units.During the second quarter, wind power generation stood at 155 million units, up 17 per cent YoY, in line with wind velocity and weather patterns.The company said the production performance reflected continued operational improvement, with higher mined metal output and additional refined metal capacity contributing to the quarterly and first-half production levels. articles.title: 251 luxury watches stolen from Rolex store in Jaipur
articles.description: More than 250 luxury watches were allegedly stolen from a Rolex showroom in Jaipur’s Tonk Road early Thursday, police said.
articles.articleText: More than 250 luxury watches were allegedly stolen from a Rolex showroom in Jaipur’s Tonk Road early Thursday, police said. The incident took place at a showroom under the Bajaj Nagar police station area, with more than five persons suspected to be involved in the burglary, they said. According to police, CCTV footage from the showroom shows two masked men removing the displayed watches and stuffing them in bags inside the store, while three to four others are seen waiting outside. The entire burglary was carried out in about 36 minutes, they said, adding that the accused allegedly broke the showroom shutter using an iron rod and entered the premises. Police said around 251 watches are reported stolen. CCTV footage from the showroom and nearby areas is being examined to identify the accused and the routes they may have taken, police said. The newspaper is run by a five-member Trust, which is chaired by Shri N N Vohra, former Governor of J&K State (2008-2018); as well as Justice S S Sodhi, former Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court; Shri Gurbachan Jagat, former Governor of Manipur; Lt Gen. Shamsher Singh Mehta, former Western Army Commander; Shri Paramjit Singh Patwalia, Senior Advocate in the Supreme Court.THE TRIBUNE is free, objective, and independent. Restraint and moderation, rather than agitational language, are the hallmarks of the paper.The Tribune has two sister publications, Punjabi Tribune (in Punjabi) and Dainik Tribune (in Hindi). articles.articleText: Exclusive Allied Industries 7 min read CenturyPly plans ₹200 crore capital expenditure in FY27; ₹250-350 crore in FY28 CenturyPly is targeting revenue of ₹10,000-12,000 crore by 2031 and plans to invest about ₹2,500 crore over five years to expand capacity, said Nikita Agarwal Bansal, executive director, CenturyPly. The company plans about ₹200 crore capex in FY27 and ₹250-350 crore subsequently for plywood expansion, while aiming to raise its share of the overall plywood market to 15% over the next four years. Ankit Sharma ETRealty Published On Oct 2, 2026 at 10:07 AM IST Representative AI imageNEW DELHI: CenturyPly is targeting revenue of ₹10,000-12,000 crore by 2031 as it plans to invest around ₹2,500 crore over five years to expand manufacturing capacity across plywood, MDF and other product categories, said Nikita Agarwal Bansal, executive director, CenturyPly.The company is currently looking at about ₹200 crore of capital expenditure in FY27, followed by ₹250-350 crore for further plywood expansion.It currently has debt of around ₹1,700 crore, largely following investments in its MDF and particle board businesses. The company expects its term loans to be repaid by 2030, but does not intend to operate with zero debt as it continues to invest for growth. Advt In an exclusive interaction with Ankit Sharma of ETRealty, Bansal spoke about the company's capex pipeline, plywood market-share strategy, pressure on MDF margins, premiumisation, capacity utilisation, raw-material costs and long-term growth plans. Edited excerpts:How has FY27 started for CenturyPly?Plywood delivered growth of more than 25%. Laminates, which had been under pressure for the last two years, finally showed signs of recovery. Particle board is also doing well. We commissioned a new plant and capacity utilisation has ramped up strongly.In MDF, growth is not the concern; EBITDA margin is. It is a more commoditised market and we have to benchmark our pricing against other players, which limits our ability to pass on price increases.The advantage for us is that we operate across multiple product categories. When one product faces margin pressure, another can support profitability. Plywood, for instance, delivered around 16.5% EBITDA margin in Q1.You had refrained from giving guidance at the beginning of the year. What happened to pricing after the increase in raw-material costs?The geopolitical situation created uncertainty, so we refrained from giving guidance initially. In plywood, we took a price increase of about 7% in April. Raw-material costs had increased by around 12-13%, but we were able to pass a significant portion of that increase to customers. Advt In MDF, we initially increased prices by around 15%, but the market could not absorb the full increase and we had to roll back part of it through discounts. The net impact was around 6-7%.The impact is more on EBITDA than on revenue.How are you protecting margins if the market does not absorb price increases?There are three factors: operating efficiencies, premiumisation and higher volumes. As utilisation at a new plant increases from, say, 50% to 65% and then 80%, fixed costs get absorbed over higher volumes. That creates operating leverage.At the same time, we are increasing the contribution of higher-value products in MDF and particle board. These products generate better margins and help offset some of the pressure from raw-material inflation.How significant is premiumisation for the MDF business?When we entered MDF, the portfolio was predominantly plain MDF. We are gradually increasing the contribution from categories such as HDF and other higher-value products. Our eventual objective is for premium products to account for around 65% of the portfolio.There can be a substantial price difference between plain MDF and higher-value products, which is why premiumisation is important from a margin perspective.What capacity additions have you made in MDF and particle board?We recently increased MDF capacity by around 67,000 CBM per annum at the Badvel plant.In particle board, we have a 2,40,000 CBM per annum plant where capacity utilisation is ramping up quarter-on-quarter. As utilisation increases, volumes rise and fixed overheads get absorbed over a larger production base.How is CenturyPly's revenue currently split across product categories?Plywood contributes around 55% of revenue. articles.title: Carlyle-led investors invest ₹2,027 crore in Nido Home Finance, acquire 58.26% stake
articles.description: Carlyle and Salisbury Investments by Aditya Puri invest ₹2,027 crore in Nido Home Finance, acquiring a majority stake and providing vital growth capital to the company.
articles.articleText: Housing Finance 2 min read Carlyle-led investors invest ₹2,027 crore in Nido Home Finance, acquire 58.26% stake Carlyle affiliate CA Sardo Investments and Salisbury Investments have completed an investment of about ₹2,027 crore in Nido Home Finance through a mix of primary capital infusion and secondary share purchase. The buyers currently hold 58.26% in Nido, which will increase to 72.70% on a fully diluted basis within 18 months. Ankit Sharma ETRealty Published On Sep 26, 2026 at 08:56 AM IST Representative AI imageNEW DELHI: Carlyle affiliate CA Sardo Investments and Salisbury Investments, an investment vehicle of Aditya Puri and his family, have completed an investment of over ₹2,000 crore in Nido Home Finance through a combination of primary capital infusion and secondary share purchase, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing.The buyers have acquired 45% of Nido’s paid-up equity share capital from Edelweiss Financial Services, Edelweiss Rural & Corporate Services and Edel Finance Company for an aggregate consideration of about ₹580.68 crore.Nido has also issued 2.59 crore equity shares and 5.18 crore warrants to the buyers for an aggregate amount of approximately ₹1,446.14 crore. The two components together translate into an investment of about ₹2,026.82 crore. Advt Following the share sale and equity allotment, the buyers currently hold 58.26% in Nido. Their stake is expected to increase to 72.70% on a fully diluted basis within 18 months following conversion of the warrants.Consequently, Nido has ceased to be a subsidiary of Edelweiss.The sellers currently hold 38.91% in Nido and their stake will reduce to 25.46% on a fully diluted basis after conversion of the warrants.₹1,446 crore primary infusionOf the total investment, approximately ₹1,446 crore represents primary capital infusion into Nido. Around ₹725 crore has already been received, while the balance is expected to be infused within 18 months. The fresh capital is expected to increase its net worth to approximately ₹2,300 crore over the next 18 months.Edelweiss said the transaction will provide Nido with growth capital while enabling the group to monetise part of its stake and reduce debt. It will also be entitled to a share of the upside if Carlyle realises returns above a specified threshold on its investment in Nido.Nido Home Finance, established in 2010, provides housing finance across affordable and mid-ticket segments. The company had assets-under-management (AUM) of approximately ₹4,900 crore as of the quarter ended June 2026 and operates through a branch network covering more than 800 talukas. articles.title: ED arrests Ozone Urbana Infra Developer's CMD in ₹927.22 crore homebuyer alleged fraud case
articles.description: The Enforcement Directorate has arrested S Vasudevan, CMD of Ozone Urbana Infra Developers, for allegedly defrauding homebuyers of ₹927.22 crore. Ongoing investigations reveal...
articles.articleText: Regulatory 3 min read ED arrests Ozone Urbana Infra Developer's CMD in ₹927.22 crore homebuyer alleged fraud case Vasudevan was arrested on September 30 under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with the money laundering investigation being conducted against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and Others. ANI Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 08:12 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday said it had arrested S Vasudevan, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) and promoter of Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, in connection with an alleged homebuyer fraud case worth Rs 927.22 crore.Vasudevan was arrested on September 30 under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with the money laundering investigation being conducted against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and Others.The Enforcement Directorate said the arrest followed an ongoing investigation which revealed that Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, along with Vasudevan (main promoter), has defrauded the home buyers to the tune of Rs 927.22 crores and did not deliver possession of apartments and units against the money, thereby dishonestly retaining and diverting the funds. Advt ED's Bengaluru Zonal Office arrested Vasudevan and subsequently produced him before a special court in Bengaluru on October 1, which granted 14 days' ED custody for further investigation.ED investigation was initiated based on multiple First Information Reports (FIRs) under sections 419, 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at various police stations of Bengaluru City against Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd and its promoters. Further, an FIR was also registered against the company and its promoter by the Central Bureau of Investigation on the direction of the Supreme Court.ED said the main allegation against the company Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd is that it has defaulted in completion of construction of the project in time and failed to hand over the possession to the customers."It is alleged that the company induced the gullible customer by offering to pay pre-construction EMIs till handing over the possession of the flat to homebuyers. However, it has failed to honour its commitments and did not complete the project and flats. The builder neither delivered possession of the residential units to homebuyers nor refunded their deposited amount and misappropriated the entire upfront booking amount/loan amount," said the ED in a statement. Advt Earlier, ED's Bangalore zonal office had conducted search operations under section 17 of PMLA, 2002 on August 1 last year in this case and seized various incriminating documents from various premises."Further investigation has revealed that Ozone Urbana Infra Developers Pvt Ltd along with Vasudevan (main promoter) have defrauded the home buyers to the tune of Rs 927.22 Crores and did not deliver possession of apartments and units against the said money, thereby dishonestly retaining and diverting the funds."Based on the investigation conducted and the material gathered, ED said it had earlier issued a Provisional Attachment Order on October 4 last year, provisionally attaching immovable properties having a total value of Rs 423.378 crores under the provisions of the PMLA.A parallel investigation has been initiated under the provisions of the PMLA, 2002 on the basis of three different FIRs registered by the CBI, New Delhi, against Ozone Infra Developers Pvt Ltd, Ozone Realtors Pvt Ltd and Ozone Projects Pvt Ltd for defrauding the homebuyers.ED said Vasudevan is the common director in all three companies under investigation.As per the ED, the arrest of Vasudevan has been effected pursuant to the material gathered during the investigation and is aimed at further investigating the generation, diversion, layering and utilisation of the Proceeds of Crime, including the role of the promoter and the various group entities and persons through whom the funds were routed. articles.title: Crib App acquires CirclePe
articles.description: Crib App has acquired CirclePe, enabling innovative rental financing solutions for tenants and property operators, eliminating the need for upfront deposits.
articles.articleText: Startups 1 min read Crib App acquires CirclePe Crib App has acquired rent financing company CirclePe to integrate deposit-free renting and upfront operator financing into its property management platform. CirclePe had raised about ₹7.5 crore in May 2024 at a valuation of around ₹35 crore. Online Bureau ETRealty Published On Jul 1, 2026 at 12:30 PM IST NEW DELHI: Crib App, a property management platform for co-living spaces, hostels and paying guest accommodations, has acquired CirclePe, a rent financing company.The acquisition will allow Crib to integrate rental financing into its platform, enabling tenants to move in without an upfront deposit while operators receive rent and deposit-linked financing upfront.CirclePe was founded by Navan Jaiswal and Ankur Yadav. In May 2024, the company had raised about ₹7.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round at a valuation of around ₹35 crore.It partners with non-banking financial companies to finance deposit or rent commitments. The amount is disbursed upfront to the operator, while the tenant repays in smaller monthly instalments. Advt Sunny Garg, co-founder and CEO, Crib said the integration will allow tenants to move in with zero deposit and operators to get paid upfront on the same platform. articles.title: Ex-CBI director M Nageswara Rao takes charge as Sarvajan Sanatan Party national president
articles.description: Rao, who served for nearly four decades in security, law and order, and administration, announced his new role while addressing a press conference in Varanasi on Saturday.
articles.articleText: Ex-CBI director M Nageswara Rao takes charge as Sarvajan Sanatan Party national presidentRao, who served for nearly four decades in security, law and order, and administration, announced his new role while addressing a press conference in Varanasi on Saturday.Published on: Oct 3, 2026, 17:56:50 ISTBy HT Correspondent, VARANASIPrefer HTon GoogleShare viaCopy link Former CBI director M Nageswara Rao has taken over as national president of the Sarvajan Sanatan Party (SSP). The party’s office-bearers elected him to the post.Ex-CBI director M Nageswara Rao addressing a press conference in Varanasi on Saturday. (HT PHOTO)Rao, who served for nearly four decades in security, law and order, and administration, announced his new role while addressing a press conference in Varanasi on Saturday.He described his entry into active politics as a new responsibility in his public life. Having closely observed the administrative system, he said he had entered politics to put his experience to use for the larger interests of the nation and society.Rao said, “Satya Sanatan, Nitya Nutan is not merely a slogan but the foundation of his vision.” He said Sanatan was not limited to a form of worship, but represented a worldview rooted in truth, righteousness (Dharma), duty, justice, compassion and public welfare.“Let us build a modern India without severing ties with our roots. In our pursuit of development, we must not lose sight of our civilizational heritage. Future generations should understand and value the rich tradition they have inherited,” Rao said.Describing Kashi as the starting point of his political journey, Rao said the city symbolised India’s civilizational continuity. He said his aim was not to return to the past but to build a modern India rooted in its civilizational heritage.Nageswara Rao was accompanied by Sarvajan Sanatan Party national vice-president Shrimahant Tirthanand, vice-president Ritu Rathore, general secretary Raja Saksham Singh Yogi, spokesperson Babita Sharma, UP in-charge Rakesh Tiwari and organisation secretary Nar-Narayan Singh.On choosing Kashi to begin political journey, Rao said the city was the “civilizational capital of Bharat”. He said his aim was not to return to the past, but to build the India of the future while remaining rooted in its civilizational heritage, which he said needed to be revived and strengthened.Rao hails from Warangal district in Telangana and holds a postgraduate degree in Chemistry. He was allotted the IPS cadre and served in various capacities during his career, eventually rising to become interim CBI director.Home/Cities/Others/Ex-CBI Director M Nageswara Rao Takes Charge As Sarvajan Sanatan Party National PresidentBy HT Correspondent, VARANASIFormer CBI director M Nageswara Rao has taken over as national president of the Sarvajan Sanatan Party (SSP). The party’s office-bearers elected him to the post.Ex-CBI director M Nageswara Rao addressing a press conference in Varanasi on Saturday. (HT PHOTO)

articles.title: Cannabis extract worth ₹1 crore concealed in cosmetic jars seized at Pune airport
articles.description: The recovered substance, weighing 1.243 kg and having an estimated value of around ₹1 crore, has been seized under provisions of the (NDPS) Act, 1985.
articles.articleText: Cannabis extract worth ₹1 crore concealed in cosmetic jars seized at Pune airportThe recovered substance, weighing 1.243 kg and having an estimated value of around ₹1 crore, has been seized under provisions of the (NDPS) Act, 1985.Published on: Oct 3, 2026, 12:22:42 ISTBy Shrinivas DeshpandePrefer HTon GoogleShare viaCopy link Pune Customs officials, in coordination with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Pune Regional Unit, seized 1.243 kg of suspected cannabis extract (hashish), allegedly concealed inside cosmetic jars at Pune International Airport on Thursday.Officers allegedly found a waxy, semi-solid substance with a pungent odour concealed inside three commercial cosmetic containers. (Hindustan Times)According to Pune Customs, the seizure followed behavioural profiling and screening of suspicious check-in baggage. Officers of the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU), Pune Customs, and DRI intercepted an Indian woman passenger who arrived at the airport from Bangkok via Air India Express flight IX-241 on the evening of October 1.During a detailed examination of her baggage, officers allegedly found a waxy, semi-solid substance with a pungent odour concealed inside three commercial cosmetic containers.Two of the containers were labelled as Rice and Yolk Hair Treatment, while the third was labelled as ‘Body Scrub’, officials said. The containers were allegedly used to camouflage the suspected narcotic substance as ordinary personal care products.A preliminary test conducted using a Narcotic Drug Field Testing Kit returned a positive result for cannabis, according to Customs officials.The recovered substance, weighing 1.243 kg and having an estimated value of around ₹1 crore, has been seized under provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.The passenger has been arrested under the relevant provisions of the NDPS Act, and further investigation is underway to ascertain the source of the contraband and its intended destination, officials said.PuneDrugsNarcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances (ndps) ActNdps ActHome/Cities/Pune News/Cannabis Extract Worth ₹1 Crore Concealed In Cosmetic Jars Seized At Pune AirportSee LessHome/Cities/Pune News/Cannabis Extract Worth ₹1 Crore Concealed In Cosmetic Jars Seized At Pune AirportBy Shrinivas DeshpandePune Customs officials, in coordination with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Pune Regional Unit, seized 1.243 kg of suspected cannabis extract (hashish), allegedly concealed inside cosmetic jars at Pune International Airport on Thursday.Officers allegedly found a waxy, semi-solid substance with a pungent odour concealed inside three commercial cosmetic containers. articles.title: Bengaluru woman takes over 3 hours to cover 19 km in peak traffic: ‘Huge respect for people who do this daily’
articles.description: A Bengaluru woman took three hours to travel 19 km amid heavy rain and traffic while rushing to catch a train. | Trending
articles.articleText: Bengaluru woman takes over 3 hours to cover 19 km in peak traffic: ‘Huge respect for people who do this daily’A Bengaluru woman took three hours to travel 19 km amid heavy rain and traffic while rushing to catch a train.Published on: Oct 3, 2026, 14:36:40 ISTBy Mahipal Singh ChouhanPrefer HTon GoogleShare viaCopy link A Bengaluru woman has shared how a 19-km journey to catch a train turned into a three-hour ordeal amid peak-hour traffic and heavy rain in the city.A Bengaluru woman recounted how a 19-km journey took three hours, leaving her racing against time to catch her train. (Instagram/heyitsilpa_)Taking to Instagram, Silpa recounted her journey from Electronic City to Krishnarajapuram railway station, saying the experience gave her a new appreciation for people who endure long commutes in Bengaluru every day.19 km in three hours“I have huge respect for people who commute long distances in Bangalore for work, in the peak Bangalore traffic moments,” she said.Silpa said she had a train to catch at 7 pm and left home at around 5 pm. The train was already running two hours late, but persistent rain worsened traffic conditions and slowed down the journey considerably.“My bad luck, it was pouring yesterday in Bangalore, so obviously the traffic was even worse, and it took us more than 3 hours to reach from Electronic City to Krishnarajapuram station, exactly 19 km in 3 hours,” she said.At one point, Silpa said she had almost given up hope of making it to the station on time. However, after noticing that the train was also being held up at different stations, she decided to continue.“We were like head-on-head with the train, kind of. So, we reached the station, we were getting off the cab, and the train was getting announced on platform number two,” she recalled.What followed was a frantic dash through the station. “We were like running with our suitcases up the stairs and down the stairs as if we were running for our life,” she said.‘Huge respect’ for daily commutersSilpa said travelling that day was important because getting another ticket to Kerala during the long weekend would have been difficult.After finally boarding the train, she said the experience made her appreciate those who regularly spend hours travelling to and from work.(Also read: Bengaluru rain chaos: City battles waterlogging, traffic snarls. Frustrated commuters share videos)“Huge respect to people who do this on a regular basis, because honestly, I am not someone who can do this every day,” she said.She also expressed hope for better transport and road infrastructure in Bengaluru, adding, “But whatever I complain about Bangalore, I still love you, Bangalore.”Sharing the clip, she wrote, “19 km. 3 hours. One train to catch. And approximately 17 emotional breakdowns in between.”Silpa later clarified in the comments that her post was not intended as an attack on the city. “Not everything on social media is an attack. Sometimes, a person is just sharing what happened to them,” she wrote.Watch the clip here: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Silpa | Intentional living (@heyitsilpa_) Internet reactsThe post drew several reactions. One user wrote, “Three hours for 19 km is unbelievable.” Another said, “Bangalore traffic really tests your patience.” A third commented, “Peak-hour traffic here is no joke.” Another added, “This is painfully relatable for commuters.”(Also read: ‘I did not see a single traffic police’: Bengaluru commuter vents after 3-hour journey)HT.com has reached out to the user for her comments, and the copy will be updated once her response is received.(Disclaimer: This report is based on user-generated content from social media. HT.com has not independently verified the claims and does not endorse them.)ABOUT THE AUTHORMahipal Singh ChouhanMahipal Singh Chouhan is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times Digital, with nearly five years of experience in digital journalism and content production. He primarily covers offbeat, trending and human-interest stories, with a focus on emerging social media trends, online conversations and real-world incidents that capture public attention. At Hindustan Times, Mahipal works on identifying and developing fast-moving digital stories, adding context and journalistic perspective to viral moments while maintaining accuracy, clarity and readability for online audiences. Before joining Hindustan Times Digital, he was associated with DNA India, where he gained experience in newsroom workflows and digital storytelling. He holds a degree in Journalism and Mass Communication from the Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies, Delhi. Beyond journalism, he has a keen interest in history and sports and enjoys expanding his general knowledge.Read MoreDiscover the latest Trending News, viral videos, social media stories and unusual events from India and around the world. The T20 World Cup 2026 tournament officially kicks off on February 7, 2026, and the final will be played on March 8, 2026. The 2026 T20 World Cup is being co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka. Matches will be held across five venues in India and three in Sri Lanka. A total of 20 teams are competing. They are divided into four groups of five. The top two teams from each group will advance to the Super 8 stage, followed by the semi-finals and the grand final. The final is scheduled to take place on March 8 at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad (subject to final qualification scenarios). You can follow every ball, wicket, and boundary on Cricket Live Score page by Hindustan Times, which features real-time updates, win probabilities, and detailed player stats. India is placed in Group A and will play four matches in the opening round. They begin their campaign against the USA on February 7 in Mumbai, followed by a match against Namibia on February 12 in Delhi. The highly anticipated clash against Pakistan will take place on February 15 in Colombo, and they will wrap up the group stage against the Netherlands on February 18 in Ahmedabad. Following the World Cup and the IPL, India has a busy bilateral schedule. In June, they host Afghanistan for a one-off Test and three ODIs. In July, India travels to England for a high-profile white-ball tour consisting of five T20Is and three ODIs. August sees a two-Test tour of Sri Lanka, followed by a series in Bangladesh in September. India will host the West Indies in September for three ODIs and five T20Is. To close out the year, they will embark on a full tour of New Zealand in October and November (Tests, ODIs, and T20Is) before returning home to host Sri Lanka for a limited-overs series in December. Several major rivalries will be renewed this year. New Zealand tours England for a Test series in June, while Australia travels to Bangladesh that same month. In the latter half of the year, Australia will head to South Africa for a crucial three-match Test series, and England will tour Australia for a white-ball series starting in November.
