articles.title: Office, mall occupancies likely to approach 90% by March 2027: Report
articles.description: Office Market Occupancy: A new ICRA report forecasts that occupancy levels for office spaces and retail malls in India will approach 90% by March 2027, driven by robust leasing...
articles.articleText: Commercial 1 min read Office, mall occupancies likely to approach 90% by March 2027: Report Occupancy across India’s top office markets is expected to reach 88.5-89% by March 2027, while Grade A malls are likely to maintain occupancy of around 88-88.5%, supported by GCC-led office demand, retailer expansion and healthy leasing activity. Online Bureau ETRealty Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 09:10 AM IST Representative AI imageNEW DELHI: Occupancy levels across office and retail mall assets are expected to move closer to 90% by March 2027, supported by healthy leasing demand, rental escalations and improving operating performance, according to a report by ICRA.India’s top six office markets recorded net absorption of about 70 million sq ft in FY26, higher than new supply of 57.8 million sq ft, which helped reduce vacancy to 12.2% from 14.1% a year earlier.Despite an expected 58-60 million sq ft of fresh office supply in FY27, continued demand from global capability centres (GCCs), flexible workspace operators and domestic corporates is expected to push office occupancy to 88.5-89% and reduce vacancy to 11-11.5% by March 2027. Advt GCC expansion is expected to remain a key driver of office leasing, particularly across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi-NCR, as global companies continue to expand technology, engineering and artificial intelligence-led operations in India.In retail real estate, vacancy across Grade A malls is expected to remain at 11.5-12% in FY27, despite the addition of 3.5-4 million sq ft of new supply.Around 35% of the upcoming retail supply has already been pre-leased, which is expected to support occupancy levels alongside continued expansion by retailers.Improving footfalls and consumption across categories such as fashion, electronics, food and entertainment are also expected to support tenant performance and leasing activity.Rental income and net operating income of mall operators are projected to grow 9.5-10% in FY27, supported by contracted rental escalations, lease renewals and sustained tenant sales.The credit profiles of office developers and mall operators are also expected to remain stable during FY27, aided by NOI growth, resilient occupancies and comfortable leverage and debt-service metrics.During the first five months of FY27, the sector recorded nine rating upgrades against one downgrade, according to the report. articles.title: Goa’s Calangute-Candolim belt to get 15 MLD water treatment plant
articles.description: 15 MLD Water Treatment Plant: New Boa Viagem pumping station and 15 MLD Pilerne WTP to ease Calangute–Candolim water shortages; locals still sceptical amid Tillari constraints...
articles.articleText: Urban Infrastructure 1 min read Goa’s Calangute-Candolim belt to get 15 MLD water treatment plant A new pumping station at Boa Viagem will feed the Pilerne plant with Tillari water, with the project expected to improve supply to Calangute, Candolim, Baga and nearby areas facing persistent shortages. TIL Creatives TNN Published On Oct 3, 2026 at 03:39 PM IST A new 15 MLD water treatment plant at Pilerne is expected to improve water supply across Goa’s Calangute-Candolim belt.The inauguration of a new water pumping station at Boa Viagem, Calangute, on Oct 7, followed by the start of a 15 MLD water treatment plant (WTP) at Pilerne, is expected to address long-standing water shortages across the Calangute–Candolim coastal belt.Calangute MLA Michael Lobo said raw water from Tillari will be pumped from Boa Viagem station to the new WTP at the Pilerne industrial estate. “Once the plant is commissioned, regular supply is expected for Candolim, Pilerne, Betim, Verem, Nerul and Calangute, areas that currently face irregular or inadequate supply. Advt Despite being a major tourism hub, Calangute has faced persistent shortages.Panchayat member Sapnesh Vaingankar said that parts of Khobravaddo and the Calangute–Baga beach belt have been getting potable water every two days, after years of erratic supply that often came once a week.A hotelier said in certain areas of Baga, water supply remains nonexistent because of blocked and ruptured pipelines in sandy, saline soil. Tanker supplies and illegal borewells meet most of the water needs.A water tank built beneath the old PWD overhead tank at Umtawaddo to improve supply has also been a point of dispute. AAP vice-president Manuel Cardozo said the tank remains unused even 12 years after completion due to lack of water, while sarpanch Joseph Sequeira disputed the claim.A new water tank is also being built in Saipem, Candolim. However, the Pilerne WTP was planned when Tillari water was surplus. With the situation changed, locals and trade remain sceptical about regular water supply. Deficient rainfall has also added to their fears.Meanwhile, activists continue to demand restrictions on large new constructions until water, electricity, and sewage systems are fully upgraded. Former panchayat member Sudesh Mayekar said development cannot continue without fixing basic services.
